content.comment_body: I am working with a [product_name] controller (version [article_no]), and I have three types of analog values I need to connect to an analog output. For example, when input 1 is activated, the analog output should deliver 5V DC; when input 2 is activated, it should deliver 7V DC from the same analog output.
Hi [user_name], Consider using an analog multiplexer function. This could help you solve your issue.

Hello [user_name], I've attached a simple example. Using an analog multiplexer allows you to output up to five values depending on input states: - No input active = 0 - Only input 1 active = 1 (can be customized) - Only input 2 active = 2 (can be customized) - Only input 3 active = 3 (can be customized) - Only input 4 active = 4 (can be customized) The example values are for demonstration; you can set them as needed in the configuration block. For reference, the analog output provides 10.00V at 1000 units, so 5V = 500 units and 7V = 700 units.

Thank you for your response; your explanation is clear. One more question: Suppose I have four inputs and one analog output. Each input corresponds with a fixed DC voltage: - I1: 2V DC - I2: 3V DC - I3: 4V DC - I4: 5V DC If I1 & I2 are activated, output should be 5V DC. If I1 & I3 are activated, output should be 6V DC. If I1 & I4 are activated, output should be 7V DC. If I2 & I3 are activated, output should be 5V DC. If I2 & I4 are activated, output should be 8V DC. If I3 & I4 are activated, output should be 9V DC. Can you explain how to configure the analog output for these input combinations?
This approach is one example. If you only want one input active for the analog multiplexer, the inputs need to be interlocked.
Is it possible to provide a sample program for this setup?
An attached file contains a possible solution.
